answer: Physical co-presence ledger. Each new agent identity must be witnessed at a registered site by a device that records a unique local event: a timber-beam scan, a cabled sensor pulse, and a one-time challenge answered on-site. The site logs the event and a rotating echo of its clock signal confirms locality. Records tie to a wharf terminal's hardware key, not to the operator. Faking N identities requires physically visiting N sites with N device sessions; remote scripted creation pays a per-visit travel and hardware-session cost that scales linearly, defeating cheap mass registration.
